items.name: Banana Date Porridge
items.description: Hearty winter-warmer — Medjool dates, banana & steel-cut oats. Natural sweetness, no sugar needed
ingredients: ½–1 Medjool date, according to preferred sweetness
steps: Remove the stone from the date. Peel the banana, slice off one third and set aside with a small sliver of the date; these will be used to finish the porridge.

Chop the remaining date and banana very finely. Place in a small pan and pour on 185ml boiling water (Rupi never uses boiling water, and the recipe turns out fine. She puts 185ml of water straight from the tap into the pan). Cook over a low heat until you have a thick, mushy, reasonably smooth paste, stirring regularly and using the back of the spoon to crush any lumps; this should take around 10 minutes. You can also use a stick blender to deal with any stubborn lumps.
While the banana-date mixture is cooking, pour the milk into a bowl, tip in the oats and leave to soak for a few minutes.
When the banana-date mix is ready, add the milk and oats to the pan, bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 12–15 minutes, stirring regularly, until the oats are completely tender.
Slice the remaining third of the banana and finely shred the reserved sliver of date. Serve the porridge in a warmed bowl, topped with the banana slices and dates.

items.name: Turkish Eggs
items.description: Poached eggs on garlicky labneh with chili oil, red pepper flakes, flaky salt & herbs, with buttered sourdough
ingredients: 1 cup labneh (or thick, strained Greek yogurt)
2 tbsp chili oil made with olive oil (such as Calabrian chili oil)
Chopped fresh dill or parsley leaves, for garnish
Sourdough or other bread of your choice, plus butter, for serving
steps: Bring a medium saucepan of water to a simmer over medium heat. Add the 2 tbsp vinegar.
Prepare the labneh: in a small bowl, stir the labneh (or yogurt) together with the garlic. Divide it between two plates, using the back of a spoon to spread it out.

One by one, crack each egg through a fine-mesh sieve. Make sure there is a bowl underneath the sieve to collect the liquid that comes through. This allows the thin, watery part of the white to drain through. This thin, watery part is what turns into wispy white strands in the pot, and we don't want that. Gently tip the egg from the sieve into a small cup or ramekin, taking care not to break the yolk.

When the water is gently simmering, not boiling (boiling or strongly simmering water won't make a proper poached egg, so turn the heat down if it starts to boil), swirl a wooden spoon in the pot to create a little tornado. While the water is swirling, gently slide one egg in, then follow with another. Two eggs max in the pot at one time. Set a timer for 3 minutes (3 minutes for a runny yolk, 3½ minutes for a jammy egg).
When the timer goes off, lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon and rest them on a paper towel, then place them on the labneh. Repeat with the rest of the eggs, 3 per plate.
Once all the eggs are on their plates, scatter over the herbs, drizzle with the chili oil, and sprinkle with red pepper flakes, flaky salt and pepper.
Warm the sourdough (or bread of your choice), butter it and serve alongside.
